title: IP4 Intermediate Mathematics · End-of-Year Examination practice paper
subtitle_note: Newly written questions in the style of a Temasek Junior College IP4 Intermediate Mathematics End-of-Year paper. Not a past-year paper.
solver_scope: O-Level Mathematics (4052) methods as taught in an IP Year 4 course — no calculus, no Additional Mathematics identities
instructions: Write your name, CG and tutor's name on all the work you hand in.
Write in dark blue or black pen. You may use a soft pencil for any diagrams or graphs.
Do not use paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid.
Answer all questions. Write your answers in the spaces provided in the question paper.
You may request for additional writing materials if there is insufficient space. These should be attached to the back of the booklet.

Give non-exact numerical answers correct to 3 significant figures, or 1 decimal place in the case of angles in degrees, unless a different level of accuracy is specified in the question. The calculator value for $\pi$ should be used unless the question requires the answer in terms of $\pi$.
The use of an approved scientific and/or graphing calculator is expected where appropriate.
You are reminded of the need for clear presentation in your answers. Marks will be deducted for poor or unclear presentation.
The number of marks is given in brackets [ ] at the end of each question or part question.
formulae: Curved surface area of a cone $= \pi r l$
Surface area of a sphere $= 4\pi r^2$
Volume of a cone $= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$
Arc length $= r\theta$, where $\theta$ is in radians
Sector area $= \dfrac{1}{2} r^2 \theta$, where $\theta$ is in radians
Standard deviation $= \sqrt{\dfrac{\sum fx^2}{\sum f} - \left(\dfrac{\sum fx}{\sum f}\right)^2}$

slots.content: (a) Simplify an expression with fractional AND negative indices in two variables to a single term (2023 did two of these; keep one). (b) Solve an equation where a PRODUCT of powers of related bases (8, 4, √2) is written as a single power of 2 — linear in x. Not a sum of powers (2023, 2024) and not a quadratic in 3^x (2025).

A Singapore context with two priced items and two sellers or two days (2025: puff stalls). (i) Form and simplify one equation — 'show that it simplifies to'. (ii) Form the second from a comparison statement (a multiple, a difference). (iii) Solve. (iv) A DECISION that uses the solution: which of two options earns more, or how many more days until a target is reached. Different context from food: tickets, an e-book vs print bundle, a class fund-raiser.

Graphing calculators NOT allowed (TJC's wording). A quadratic with a NEGATIVE leading coefficient other than −3. (i) Complete the square; state the coordinates of the turning point and whether it is a maximum or minimum. (ii) Sketch the graph, labelling turning point and the intercepts with both axes (roots exact or 2 d.p.). (iii) State, with a reason from the sketch, the values of k for which the line y = k meets the curve at two points. 2025 met a line and asked about tangency; 2024 solved an inequality; this asks about a horizontal line.

(a) Solve a DOUBLE linear inequality with fractional coefficients (2025's was quadratic) and represent the solution on a number line. (b) Hence write down the integer values of x in the solution, and the largest possible value of a stated expression such as x² or 5 − 2x.

Roles swapped from 2025 (which showed y = axⁿ and asked to sketch 1/x + 2). (a) A sketch of a RECIPROCAL curve y = a/xⁿ is shown passing through a labelled point: write down n and find a. (b) Sketch y = 3^x − 2 (an exponential shifted down) on the axes provided, labelling the y-intercept, the x-intercept to 2 d.p. and the equation of the asymptote. The figure is the given sketch for (a); the axes for (b) are answer space.

A figure of two triangles sharing a vertex with a pair of PARALLEL sides (not 2025's trapezium-with-perpendicular, not 2024's angle-bisector isosceles). (i) Prove the two triangles are similar, a reason for each statement. (ii) Given one length ratio and the area of the smaller triangle, find the area of the trapezium or quadrilateral between them. (iii) A second pair of triangles in the same figure share a height: state the ratio of their areas from a ratio of bases, with a reason. The (iii) idea — equal heights, not similarity — is the change.

A 2×2 matrix method in a context with TWO unknown unit prices (2025 was a 3×3 with a graphing calculator; 2024 durians by 2×2 — so change the direction): the totals are given for two customers. (i) Write the matrix equation PQ = R. (ii) Find P⁻¹ and hence Q. (iii) Write a row matrix S such that SQ gives a stated total for a third customer, and evaluate it. Context away from food and fruit: stationery for two classes, MRT + bus fares, two sizes of a print order.

Right-angled trigonometry in a built setting (2025: playground slide; 2023: towns by bearings). A building with a flagpole/antenna on top, viewed from a point on level ground: two angles of elevation given (to the top of the building and to the top of the pole). (i) Show the height of the building to 3 s.f. (ii) Find the height of the pole. (iii) The viewer moves a stated distance closer/further: find the new angle of elevation of the top of the pole. Figure with the two elevation lines.

Bearings with the sine/cosine rule and a CLOSEST-APPROACH idea, not tested in 2023–2025. A ship (or drone) travels from A to B; a lighthouse L is at a given bearing and distance from A. (i) Find angle LAB from the bearings. (ii) Find LB by the cosine rule. (iii) Find the SHORTEST distance from L to the path AB, and hence the GREATEST angle of elevation of the top of the lighthouse (height given) seen from the ship on that path.

A composite solid where the quantity asked is SURFACE AREA (2025 asked volume of a bottle; 2023 asked surface area of a cone-hemisphere, so choose a different composite): a cylinder with a hemispherical hollow scooped from one end and a cone on the other, OR a frustum-topped cylinder — dimensions given, one length to be found by Pythagoras first. (i) Find the total surface area, to 3 s.f., stating which faces are included. (ii) The solid is to be painted; a tin covers a stated area; find the least number of tins (round UP) and the cost.

Two points A and B given; (i) the gradient or equation of AB. (ii) C lies on the x-axis such that angle ABC = 90°: find C (perpendicular gradients). (iii) D such that ABCD is a parallelogram: find D. (iv) Find the area of ABCD by the shoelace method, AND HENCE the perpendicular distance from D to AB — the 'hence distance' step is the change from 2025's trapezium area and 2023's rhombus. No accurate drawing accepted.

Abstract vectors a and b in a PARALLELOGRAM OABC (2025: triangle with a constant k; 2024: column vectors in a quadrilateral). M is the midpoint of AB; N is on OC produced with ON : OC given. (i) OM in terms of a and b. (ii) MN in terms of a and b, simplified. (iii)(a) Show/state that MN is parallel to a named side and (iii)(b) find the ratio MN : that side, OR the ratio of the areas of two triangles in the figure.

(a) TWO INDEPENDENT trials (a spinner spun twice, or a die and a coin) — 2025 was without replacement; draw or use a possibility diagram: (a)(i) P(both the same), (a)(ii) P(sum/product is a stated value), (a)(iii) P(at least one of a kind). (b) A VENN diagram (not a two-way table) with numbers in each region for two events A and B among n people: (b)(i) P(A ∩ B'), (b)(ii) P(A ∪ B), (b)(iii) P((A ∪ B)'). Fractions in simplest form.

A shaded region formed by a SECTOR and a SEGMENT/TRIANGLE in one circle (2025: two major sectors sharing a chord; 2023 and 2024: sectors with a tangent). (i) Find the perimeter in terms of r and π exactly. (ii) Given the shaded AREA as an exact expression in π and √3, find θ (in radians) or r — the given-area-find-the-angle direction. Angle labelled in radians in the figure.

Angle chasing 'stating all reasons clearly' (TJC every year) in a NEW configuration: a cyclic quadrilateral with one side produced and a tangent at a vertex, so alternate-segment, exterior-angle-of-cyclic-quadrilateral and angles-in-the-same-segment are all needed. (i) and (ii) find two labelled angles. (iii) Find the third AND explain why a named chord IS or IS NOT a diameter (the converse of the angle in a semicircle) — the decision is the change.

(a) A misleading chart — a DIFFERENT fault from 2025's BTO bar chart: a line graph with a truncated vertical axis, or two pie charts of different sizes; explain how it misleads and one improvement. (b) A GROUPED FREQUENCY TABLE (2025 gave a histogram) of a measured quantity for group Alpha; group Beta is summarised by a BOX-AND-WHISKER plot with its median and IQR readable. (b)(i) Estimate the mean and standard deviation for Alpha, working shown. (b)(ii) Which group scored higher on average, with a reason. (b)(iii) Which is more consistent — compare a spread measure that BOTH have. (b)(iv) A one-line comparison the two representations allow (e.g. whether Alpha's median could be found exactly, and why not).
